source: Local news, developers and community benefits for tab sites (researched, verified, adjudicated)

sites.name: Spence Field
gaps: Searched 'Spence Field Sturgis Michigan redevelopment' and '"Spence Field" Sturgis St. Joseph County'. Results for Spence Field were a Georgia WWII airfield and a Spence Road in St. Joseph County with no field; no Sturgis, Michigan record of a site by this name was found.

Searched the record's addresses (500 McKee St, 601 N. Centerville St) with brownfield and redevelopment terms. No news, city, or county item tied to these addresses was found. A St. Joseph County brownfield document lists other Sturgis sites (Stapleton Industrial Park, Dresser Industrial Park, 201 S. Nottawa St) but not this property.
City of Sturgis and St. Joseph County Brownfield Redevelopment Authority pages were not opened; the search tool did not surface a site-specific item from them.

sites.name: Riverview Apartments
gaps: Address match: the Living New Deal entry lists the complex at 1013 Douglas Street, Kingsport, which matches the record. No city or housing-authority page giving the address was opened.

City of Kingsport ribbon-cutting (Riverview Place, 32 homes on the former Riverview Apartments site, about $8.4 million, from an $11.9 million HUD HOPE VI grant) and groundbreaking pages appeared in search results, but both returned HTTP 404 when opened, so no quote could be copied. Those facts are not included.

Kingsport Housing & Redevelopment Authority page (Riverview Place at 285 Louis St, 38 units) was opened; it does not mention Douglas Street or the HOPE VI Riverview project, and it is a different address, so it is not used.
No news item on the 2008 demolition, the HOPE VI project, or current status of the Douglas Street parcel was found.

sites.name: 35TH AVENUE

facts.summary: WBRC reported in January 2020 that cleanup remaining at the 35th Avenue Superfund site (Collegeville, Fairmont, Harriman Park, North Birmingham) was expected to take two to three years, with about 185 properties still on the cleanup list. No completion date was given.
facts.reference: New timeline released for cleaning up 35th Ave. Superfund site
facts.quote: the remainder of work is expected to take in 2 to 3 years.

facts.summary: Per WBRC, EPA's cleanup budget for the 35th Avenue residential soil project was about $40 million in total, to be spent by the end of the project. This is a cleanup commitment to residents, not a host-community payment.
facts.reference: New timeline released for cleaning up 35th Ave. Superfund site
facts.quote: they'll spend a total of $40 million by the end of the project.

facts.summary: An EPA reuse page, captured in an archived January 2025 snapshot, says EPA has cleaned up more than 650 properties at the 35th Avenue site. The page's own date is not shown; the date used is the snapshot date.
facts.authority: U.S. EPA (archived Superfund redevelopment page, Alabama)
facts.reference: Superfund sites in reuse: Alabama (archived 2025-01-19 snapshot)
facts.quote: To date, the EPA has cleaned up over 650 properties.

gaps: Searched '35th Avenue Superfund Birmingham Ensley redevelopment'. No development project, developer, or approved reuse plan for the residential Superfund area was found; the EPA reuse page describes continued residential, commercial, industrial and public-service uses without naming a project.

The Ensley High School redevelopment (2301 Ensley LP, terminated per BhamNow, Feb 2026) is a different property about 1-2 miles away and is not used. The record's point (3500 35th N.) was not matched to a specific cleanup parcel.
A 2016 EPA redevelopment grant of about $400,000 for neighborhoods within the site was reported in a search snippet, but the source page was not opened, so it is not cited.
City of Birmingham council resolution asking EPA for national priority status was mentioned in the WBRC piece but its date and text were not confirmed, so it is not cited.

sites.name: JACKSONVILLE NAVAL AIR STATION

facts.summary: Proposed, not built: in August 2016 WOKV reported the Navy was working to finalize a deal with an unnamed energy utility to develop a 50-acre solar farm on the Yellow Water Creek property at NAS Jacksonville, producing about 5 MW. The developer or utility was not named, and no later report on the deal was found. The solar parcel location was not matched to this record's point (NAS Bldg 826).
facts.reference: Navy working to bring solar power to NAS Jax community
facts.quote: The deal between the Navy and the unnamed utility would develop 50 acres of the Yellow Water Creek property.

gaps: Searched NAS Jacksonville with data center, enhanced use lease, lease, solar and redevelopment terms for 2025-2026. No Navy enhanced use lease or data center deal at NAS Jacksonville was found; the Navy data center leases in results (NAS Lemoore, Pax River) are other bases.
The solar item in the WOKV results is undated in some search copies; the 2016 date was taken from the article text when opened. Whether the solar farm was completed was not found.

The NextNRG 1,600-acre Nassau County data center and the Jacksonville Aviation Authority VanTrust lease are off-base (not NAS Jacksonville land), so they are not used. Cecil Field (former NAS Cecil, a different base) reuse results were not used.
No 2025-2026 news on the NAS Jacksonville Superfund cleanup or reuse was found.

sites.name: CAMP HALE

facts.summary: A 2015 Vail Daily report on a proposed Forest Service-led restoration of Camp Hale wetlands and floodplain, backed by the National Forest Foundation. The project manager said wetlands fell from about 450 acres to 150 acres after the camp was built, and the project could restore up to 350 acres. This is an ecological restoration proposal, not a development project. The article does not say it was funded or built.
facts.reference: Project proposed to restore Camp Hale (Melanie Wong, 2015-03-20)
facts.quote: A proposed project would help restore Camp Hale to look a bit more like it did before it had military uses.

gaps: Searched for a solar project at Camp Hale and found none. The solar results were unrelated (a Clark County, Nevada project and an Eagle County maintenance-building array in Gypsum).

The Federal Register notice withdrawing the Camp Hale Restoration and Enhancement Project EIS notice of intent (91 FR 31404, 2026-05-27) appeared in search results, but federalregister.gov redirected to an access page and the Justia mirror returned 403. Not cited. A secondary summary says the withdrawal was to re-evaluate resource needs; verify on the Federal Register itself.
No 2026 local news on the withdrawal or a replacement timeline was found.

sites.name: BUCKLEY FIELD
gaps: Searched Buckley Field and Buckley Space Force Base solar. Results on the on-base solar arrays (2009 to 2020 reports) were not cited: the FUDS record's 64,891-acre footprint is not confirmed to be the active base, and the sources disagree on output share.

Lead, not cited: Arapahoe County File 24-515 proposes a 5.0 MW solar facility on a 106.5-acre parcel north of E. Hampden Avenue and west of E-470 (applicant USS High Plains Solar LLC; owner Lowry Environmental Protection Cleanup Trust Fund), on former Lowry Bombing and Gunnery Range land. I did not open the Legistar page, could not confirm that the parcel falls within the Buckley Field FUDS record, and found no status after filing.
No other news on the Buckley Field property was found.

sites.name: FRANKFORD ARSENAL

facts.summary: Police officers filed a lawsuit in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas over illnesses they attribute to the site. It names the Philadelphia Authority for Industrial Development Cooperation, developer Mark Hankin, and Hankin's businesses. These are the plaintiffs' allegations, not findings. The article gives only 'Monday' as the filing day, so the month is taken from the 2025-12-09 publication date.
facts.reference: The Frankford Arsenal once housed Philly's narcotics unit (2025-12-09)
facts.quote: The lawsuit, filed Monday in the Philadelphia Court of Common Pleas,

facts.summary: Alliance Partners HSP reported in 2018 that it had bought six of the buildings and was restoring them as creative flex space for commercial and light-industrial tenants. The article gives square footage but no price. Current status is not confirmed.
facts.reference: The Frankford Arsenal Takes the First Steps in Its Third Life (Sandy Smith, 2018-08-06)
facts.quote: Alliance Partners HSP, which has acquired six of the buildings at the Arsenal site

facts.summary: A 2010 report that Hankin Management Co. planned a 500,000-square-foot retail center with a $50 million development price tag. The headline says demolition was clearing the way. The article names no tenant. This is a reported plan, and no later status was found.
facts.reference: Demolition Paves Way for 500,000-SF Shopping Center at Former Arsenal in Philly (2010-07-28)
facts.quote: Hankin Management Co. is behind the 500,000-square-foot retail project

facts.summary: In 2014, Councilman Bobby Henon, the Commerce Department and the Philadelphia Industrial Development Corporation were in talks with an unnamed potential industrial tenant for the former Frankford Arsenal waterfront site. PIDC described it as a manufacturing project. The tenant was not named, and no outcome was found.
facts.reference: City courting industrial tenant for Frankford Arsenal site in Bridesburg (2014-04-25)
facts.quote: The proposal is for a manufacturing project, said John Grady, executive director of PIDC.

gaps: Found 2021 coverage of Weizer Management buying Buildings 38 and 39 for shared kitchens (Northeast Times and Star News). Both pages returned 403 and the search snippets are not quotes, so nothing is cited. Verify on those pages.
A 2025 PHILADELPHIA.Today coworking-kitchen article was in search results but was not opened. Not cited.
No 2025 or 2026 coverage of Hankin's current plans for the campus was found. The 2010 retail plan and the 2014 tenant talks are the latest development plans found. Not confirmed as current.

sites.name: RIDGEWOOD ARMY WEAPONS PLANT
gaps: Searched Ridgewood Army Weapons Plant with Cincinnati and found no coverage of this site.

sites.name: PEOPLES GAS CRAWFORD STATION FORMER MGP

facts.summary: EPA said in an August 2021 release that Peoples Gas parcels G and V at 4358 W. 35th Place, part of the Crawford Station former manufactured gas plant, would be cleaned up with work starting in September 2021. The plan removes the top 4-8 feet of soil offsite and treats deeper soil in place. The release does not say the parcels are approved for reuse, and I did not find a later status update.
facts.reference: EPA news release: Work to start in September at Peoples Gas Crawford Station, Chicago (dated 2021-08-11)
facts.quote: removing the top 4-8 feet of soil and disposing it offsite.

gaps: Searched Peoples Gas Crawford Station MGP redevelopment, and the 35th Place parcels with EPA cleanup. Found no 2022-2026 news on parcel reuse or redevelopment. The EPA Crawford fact sheet and CIP PDFs returned unreadable binary, so no status or reuse plan was read from them. Not cited: the 2018 Hilco 'Crawford Station' article (Bisnow, 2018-02-07). It describes a 70-acre former coal-plant site at I-55 and Pulaski, sold by Midwest Generation to NRG, and does not mention Peoples Gas or the MGP parcels, so it is a different property. The release's 'available for reuse' language was in a search snippet, not on the page I opened, so it is not stated as fact.

sites.name: BUTTERWORTH #2 LANDFILL

facts.summary: Proposed City of Grand Rapids solar array of nearly 2 MW on the Butterworth landfill, which the city says maximizes behind-the-meter delivery. The page lists an estimated construction start of July 2026 and in-service in 2027. It does not say the array is built or energized.
facts.reference: City of Grand Rapids: Butterworth Solar Array project page
facts.quote: pursuing a nearly 2MW solar array that maximizes behind-the-meter delivery

facts.summary: The city project page says Enerlogics was selected to complete the solar installation at the Butterworth site. The page names an earlier developer, secured in 2015, which became insolvent in 2016 and whose name it does not give. The page is undated, so no date is recorded for the selection.
facts.reference: City of Grand Rapids: Butterworth Solar Array project page
facts.quote: Enerlogics selected to complete solar installation

facts.summary: Michigan Public reported that the state is providing $3 million to Grand Rapids for the infrastructure needed to carry solar electricity from the former Butterworth landfill to the city's circuit. The article says solar would sit on top of the capped landfill, because the cap prevents building into it. It names no developer and gives no construction date.
facts.reference: Michigan Public: A former Superfund landfill site in Grand Rapids is closer to providing solar power (2024-10-09)
facts.quote: The state is providing three million dollars to Grand Rapids.

gaps: Searched Butterworth Landfill Grand Rapids 1450 Butterworth redevelopment. Found the city project page and the Michigan Public article, both opened and cited. The Crain's Grand Rapids article (undated in search results) returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so nothing is cited from it. Not opened: a 2013 EPA assessment and the landfill's ownership split, and the Grand Rapids Butterworth page. Search results also cite older rugby and trail uses that I did not verify. The city page's construction dates are plans, and I found no confirmation of current construction status.

sites.name: FLAT CREEK IMM

facts.summary: Montana DEQ held a public comment meeting on Thursday, January 14, 2016, on an engineering evaluation and cost analysis for mine tailings at the Flat Creek-Iron Mountain Mine NPL site, four miles northeast of Superior. The notice covers alternatives for tailings on USFS and former ASARCO lands. It does not mention redevelopment, reuse or land transfer.
facts.reference: Montana Environmental Trust Group, DOE Seeks public comment on Flat Creek-Iron Mountain Mine (posted 2016-01-21)
facts.quote: regarding an Engineering Evaluation and Cost Analysis (EE/CA) for the Flat Creek-Iron Mountain Mine

facts.summary: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service opened a 30-day public comment period, March 19 to April 18, 2026, on a draft restoration plan for natural resource injuries from historic mining. The page title names the Flat Creek/Iron Mountain Mine and Mill Superfund site together with Black Pine Mine. The quoted text does not name Flat Creek, so the link to this site rests on the page title. This is a federal natural resource notice, not a redevelopment action.
facts.authority: U.S. Department of the Interior, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
facts.reference: DOI, Draft Restoration Plan Released for Black Pine Mine and Flat Creek/Iron Mountain Mine and Mill Superfund Site, MT (2026-03-19)
facts.quote: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service) is seeking public comment on a Draft Restoration Plan to address injuries

gaps: No developer, buyer, incentive, redevelopment project or community benefit agreement found for Flat Creek IMM in Superior. Searched the site name with Superior and Montana plus redevelopment, and the site name with 2025 cleanup news.
EPA Region 8 superfund reuse page lists 'Flat Creek IMM (Superior, MT)', but the fetched page showed no entry text for it. Not cited.
No 2025 or later cleanup news found. The EPA and Montana pages found are older documents, so the current cleanup status is not verified.
A search snippet attributed a site employment figure to an EPA economic case study. The case study was not opened, so the figure is not cited.

sites.name: DIAMOND ALKALI CO.

facts.summary: EPA finalized the cleanup plan for the 80-120 Lister Ave. portion of the Diamond Alkali Superfund site on January 17, 2025, after a September 2024 proposal. The final plan continues the existing remedy and makes repairs to the cap over contaminated materials. EPA's release does not mention redevelopment or new development on the parcels.
facts.reference: EPA, Issues Final Cleanup Plan for Lister Ave. Portion of Diamond Alkali Superfund Site, Newark (2025-01-17 release, archived on EPA's 19january2025 snapshot site)
facts.quote: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency finalized its cleanup plan for the 80-120 Lister Ave. portion

facts.summary: EPA proposed a permanent cleanup plan for the Lister Avenue portion on September 10, 2024, with a 30-day comment period to October 10, 2024 and a public meeting on September 19, 2024. The proposal keeps the existing cap and groundwater system and reactivates seven groundwater pumps. The page states the goal of protecting the people of Newark and Passaic River communities from toxic contamination.
facts.reference: EPA, Invites community feedback on proposed final cleanup plan for Lister Ave. portion of Diamond Alkali Superfund site (last updated 2024-09-10)
facts.quote: with improvements including reinstalling and reactivating a total of seven groundwater pumps

gaps: No developer, buyer, incentive, redevelopment plan or community benefit agreement found for 80 or 120 Lister Ave. Searched the address, the site name, Newark Riverfront Park and 2025 news.

An EPA Superfund Redevelopment document says cleanup paved the way for redevelopment of this property into Newark Riverfront Park. The excerpt did not confirm which parcel that refers to, so it is not cited.

East Newark Riverfront Park (ribbon-cutting May 9, 2025; 2022 DOJ interim settlement tied to Diamond Alkali) is a different property in East Newark. The NJBIZ article does not name 80 or 120 Lister Avenue, so it is not cited.
No local news found on hearings, votes, opposition or lawsuits for the Lister Avenue parcels in the search results.

EPA's 'Alternative Energy at Superfund Sites: Status Update and Highlights from Across the Country - 2024' (created 2024-12-02, semspub.epa.gov HQ/100003555) appears in search results with this site in a technology-type column marked by an asterisk. The row was not readable: no PDF text tool is installed here, and the HTML view was truncated before the table. The technology type is unconfirmed, so nothing is cited from it.

The Marine Corps article on solar at Quantico (quantico.marines.mil) could not be fetched (DNS failure). Search snippets describe a 2012 array on a Marine Helicopter Squadron 1 hangar, not an MCCDC facility. Not cited.
ProPublica's Quantico installation page lists cleanup spending for Quantico sites. It was not opened, so nothing is cited from it.
